target.title: fix(update-check): wrap malformed npm view JSON parse in try/catch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`fetchNpmPackageTargetStatus` bounds `npm view --json` stdout to 1 MiB, but when the bounded string is malformed JSON the parse failure currently surfaces as a raw `SyntaxError` string through the outer catch. That gives callers no indication the failure came from npm metadata parsing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wrapped `JSON.parse` inside `parseNpmPackageTargetMetadata` with a contextual `try/catch`. The error is rethrown with the parse cause and is then caught by the existing `fetchNpmPackageTargetStatus` catch block, so the function returns `{ version: null, nodeEngine: null, error: ... }` with a clear "npm view returned invalid JSON" message.

## User Impact

Update/status checks report clearer diagnostics when npm returns malformed metadata; it is easier to distinguish an npm-side JSON glitch from other command failures.

## Evidence

Terminal proof (after fix) uses a real fake `npm` executable on disk:

```bash
node_modules/.bin/tsx scripts/proof/update-check-malformed-npm-json.mts
```

Output:

```
=== Proof: update-check malformed npm view JSON ===

Using fake npm executable: /tmp/openclaw-proof-npm-XXXXXX/npm

Result: {
  "target": "openclaw",
  "version": null,
  "nodeEngine": null,
  "error": "Error: npm view returned invalid JSON: SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'o', \"not valid json {\" is not valid JSON"
}

PASS: malformed npm view JSON is caught and surfaced as an error.
```

Regression test:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/update-check.test.ts
```

All 32 tests pass.
